title: A Thrilling GM vs IM Blitz Match + Danya Story Time! | GM Naroditsky

moves.spoken: White pins with the bishop on b5 against the knight — the Rossolimo, a positional anti-Sicilian that swaps sharp theory for a small, controlled centre. The knight comes to f3 behind it.
teaches: The Rossolimo (Bb5 vs Nc6) is a positional anti-Sicilian

moves.spoken: Black plays e6, building a compact, flexible pawn shell.
White castles, and Black tucks the second knight on e7 — a modest square that keeps the option of rerouting to g6 or d5.
c3 — the heart of the Rossolimo plan: prepare d4 and claim the centre without ever committing to the sharp lines.
teaches: c3 prepares the d4 central break in the Rossolimo

moves.spoken: Black grabs queenside space with a6 and b5, and rather than let the bishop be harassed off the board White nurses it back — first to d3, then c2, keeping it on the long light diagonal aimed at the kingside.
teaches: Retreat the bishop to preserve it rather than let pawns chase it down

moves.spoken: Black fianchettoes with the bishop to b7, leaning on the e4-pawn along the long diagonal.
a3 quietly forbids b5-b4, denying Black the tempo and keeping the queenside clamped.
teaches: a3 takes the b4 break away from Black

moves.spoken: Black strikes in the centre with d5, challenging the e4-pawn head-on.
White meets it with d4, and the centre locks into full tension.
After the trades White recaptures with the bishop to e4 — beautifully placed, raking down the long diagonal at Black's bishop on b7 and eyeing the kingside.
Black sends the knight to the rim on a5, and the engine's needle jumps White's way: a knight on the edge of the board defends nothing and attacks little.
teaches: A knight on the rim is offside — it defends nothing and attacks little

moves.spoken: White trades the light-squared bishops, and Black is forced to recapture with the knight, leaving it stranded and passive on b7.
teaches: Trade to leave the opponent\u2019s piece passive

moves.spoken: The knight develops to c3, hitting the d5-square and joining the fight for the centre.
Black centralizes with the knight to d5 — active-looking, but White is already clearly on top, and the engine wants the outpost.

White plants the knight on e5 — a dominant central outpost the pawns can't chase away. The engine now reads it near a full pawn for White: the offside a5-b7 detour has left Black a passive game against a commanding centre.
teaches: A knight on e5 that can\u2019t be evicted is a lasting positional trump
plans: Anchor the knight on the e5 outpost
Press the space and the better-placed pieces
